title: Predictive backpressure matrix and soft‑quota lanes for prefill→decode pipeline
author: Anika Rao
description:
Motivation: We observed tail latency spikes under mixed interactive and streaming traffic during canary runs. Root cause analysis pointed to hard admission thresholds in the prefill stage that either over‑reserved KV memory and kernels or starved the decode stage under bursty arrivals. This PR introduces a predictive backpressure matrix and soft‑quota lane system that dynamically shapes admission and kernel allocation between prefill and decode to reduce stalls while preserving throughput.

Design summary: 1) Predictive backpressure matrix: a lightweight runtime component that consumes short history of per‑route arrival rate, batch sizes, and KV hit ratios to predict intra‑second demand. It computes an admission score per logical lane (latency‑sensitive, balanced, throughput) that ties into the scheduler. 2) Soft‑quota lanes: instead of hard segmented quotas, lanes have soft token buckets that allow transient overshoot with controlled decay; overshoots are reconciled by probabilistic throttling and KV admission demotion. 3) Kernel bucket scheduler: kernels are grouped into buckets by memory footprint and latency characteristics; scheduler assigns prefill and decode micro‑slices to kernel buckets based on lane scores and predicted contention. 4) KV stripe admission: KV cache admission now uses a stripe allocator that prefers admitting prefixes likely to be reused across lanes (LRU+reuse heuristic). 5) Continuous batching seam: micro‑slice boundaries are adjusted to allow cooperative coalescing across prefill→decode handoff when latency headroom exists.

Compatibility: Changes are backwards compatible at the API level. New runtime flags gate the behavior per deployment: --prefill-backpressure=adaptive and per‑route config options in the serving config to opt into soft‑quota lanes. Default is off on older clusters; enabled in canary clusters.

Checklist:
- [x] Predictive matrix proto, runtime telemetry hooks, and unit tests
- [x] Kernel bucket scheduler and integration tests
- [x] KV stripe admission and cache benchmarks
- [x] E2E canary with gradual rollout and metrics dashboard panels
- [x] Documentation updates (console and runtime flags)

Risk and mitigation: The predictive model uses only short window aggregated counters to avoid oscillation; we cap lane overshoot and enforce a global soft limit to prevent KV runaway. Rollout is staged by region and can be disabled via config.

How to validate: Follow canary playbook linked in the PR, check per‑route p50/p95/p99 latency, prefill/decode queue lengths, KV adoption ratio, and cost per 1k tokens. The PR includes Grafana dashboard diff and synthetic load scripts used in validation.

review_comments: Sophie Chen: Could predictiveness introduce oscillations under diurnal patterns? Please add damping/decay tests.
Author (Anika Rao): Added exponential decay smoothing and a cap to overshoot; added unit tests in tests/prefill_backpressure_test.cc.
Marco Alvarez: Kernel buckets look good; consider exposing a per‑bucket headroom metric for ops to tune.
Author: Exposed kernel_bucket.headroom_gauge and added dashboard tile to canary panels.
Priya Nair: KV stripe allocator needs a config knob to prefer per‑tenant isolation in Dedicated mode.
Author: Added prefer_isolation boolean in the stripe allocator config; default preserved for shared modes.
benchmark_summary: Canary against mixed interactive+streaming synthetic workload: p95 end‑to‑end latency reduced 8.6% (from 320ms→292ms), p99 improved 6.9%. Average token throughput maintained within 1% of baseline. KV cache hit ratio improved ~4% on repeat conversational workloads. Observed cost per 1k tokens reduction ~11% due to fewer wasted prefill kernels and better batching coalescing.
release_notes: Introduce runtime adaptive prefill backpressure with soft‑quota lanes and kernel bucket scheduler. Opt‑in via runtime flag --prefill-backpressure=adaptive; provides p95 latency and cost improvements for mixed workloads. Disabled by default for older clusters.
notes_for_ops: To enable in Dedicated: set serving.config.prefill_backpressure.mode=adaptive and adjust kernel_bucket.headroom per GPU class. Monitor metrics: backpressure.matrix.score, prefill.queue.length, decode.queue.length, kernel_bucket.headroom_gauge. Rollback: set mode=off and drain existing soft overshoots.
